newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Reed-Elsevier in U.S. legal buy.
newsitem.headline: Reed-Elsevier in U.S. legal buy.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch publishing group Reed-Elsevier said on Wednesday it had reached agreement with Thomson Corp to buy publishing rights to the U.S. Supreme Court Reports and some 40 other standard legal works.
Reed-Elsevier said the activities it planned to acquire were profitable and generated sales revenues in 1996 of at least 90 million guilders.
U.S. anti-trust authorities had ordered Thomson to sell off the publications in question as a condition for approval of Thomson's acquistion last year of West Publishing Co in the U.S.
Reed-Elsevier said the acquisition would be completed as soon as approval was obtained from the U.S. authorities.

It said the publications concerned were established and profitable titles which sold strongly in print and CD-ROM formats and also electronically through Reed-Elsevier's Lexis-Nexis on-line database business.

"The acquisition provides another opportunity for the company to broaden its spectrum of legal information and provide industry-leading sources, in any medium, to its customers," the group said in a statement.
"These properties which Thomson is divesting fit superbly into the Lexis-Nexis business and will enable it to serve the U.S. legal community even more effectively," it added.
